clue.text: Temple of Zeus perhaps old man guards

indicators.note: to guard something is to stand around it, so the father's letters surround the deity's

parts.note: old man is familiar slang for father, PA
Zeus is an example of a god, here A GOD

explanation.surface: A father keeps watch over a Greek god's shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zeus perhaps' gives A GOD, article included; 'guards' puts PA around it, P at the front and A at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower serving as a Buddhist or Hindu place of worship.

clue.text: Use of Latin for section in writings is commoner

indicators.note: using one letter for another in a word signals a swap, with 'for' and 'in' placing the pieces
for marks what is being replaced: the Latin letter stands in for the section letter
in names the word where the swap is made, the writings

parts.note: prose is ordinary written work

explanation.surface: A grammar note: putting Latin passages into a piece of writing makes it more common.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction reads as a recipe: in PROSE, use L instead of S.
explanation.definitionFit: A prole, short for proletarian, is a member of the working class, an ordinary commoner rather than a noble.

clue.text: Well-bred egret not regularly missing fish

indicators.note: letters missing at regular intervals leaves every other one of the words egret not

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A refined egret goes without its catch of fish now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping alternate letters of 'egret not' keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth: G, E, N, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel describes polite, refined manners associated with a respectable upbringing.

clue.text: Simple process to collar doctor over a stroke

indicators.note: to collar is to grab around the neck, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a doddle is British slang for something very easy

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the doctor above the a

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is grabbed in an easy procedure, said to be about a stroke, as in a medical stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' and 'doctor' set up a medical scene, but the stroke is a swimming one; 'to collar' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog paddle is a basic swimming stroke, the paddling action a dog uses in water.

clue.text: Save on small item one strikes with

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning
a cue is the stick used to strike the ball in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: A shopper is told to economise on a little bat or stick for hitting things.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone from danger is to come to their aid and deliver them.

clue.text: Rival discovered bits of DNA many essentially overlooked

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its covering removed, so the outer letters of the word for DNA bits go

parts.note: genes are sections of DNA

indicators.note: the essential part of a word is its middle, and overlooked means it is left out of the word many

explanation.surface: A competitor uncovered genetic material that many people had missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips GENES to ENE; 'essentially overlooked' drops the middle AN from MANY, leaving MY.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is an opponent or foe, someone set against you as a rival.

clue.text: Standard brace fixed across tips of lower incisors

indicators.note: one piece set across another spans it, so the rearranged brace letters stretch either side
fixed in the sense of adjusted or repaired, so the letters are rearranged
the tips of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An orthodontist fits a brace across the bottom front teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' reads as fitted to the teeth but signals the rearrangement CABRE; 'across' then spans the two initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means level of quality or ability, the standard someone or something reaches.

clue.text: People who praise Dead Ringers?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer living or current
tollers are those who toll, or ring, bells

explanation.surface: A cryptic question: are the satirists of Dead Ringers, a BBC impressions show, flatterers?
explanation.walkthrough: Dead Ringers is a BBC radio and TV impressions comedy, so the capitals look like a title; split it as former bell-ringers.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so extollers are those who sing someone's praises.

clue.text: Busy agent on duty for vessel

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling movement, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: An overworked agent is on duty supervising a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was a historic tax charged on ships, levied at a rate per ton of cargo capacity.

clue.text: Run down piano is in key

indicators.note: one piece being in another means it goes inside it

parts.note: Delete is a key on a computer keyboard
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pianist runs through a piece written in a particular musical key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a musical key such as D minor, but here it is the computer key.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a stock is to use it up or run it down.

clue.text: It's painful sitting inside this French compartment

indicators.note: a piece sitting inside another is placed within it

parts.note: cette is French for this, with a feminine noun
ouch is what one says when something hurts

explanation.surface: A traveller complains about an uncomfortable seat in a French railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A couchette is a sleeping berth in a train carriage, especially on continental European railways.

clue.text: A party member putting party first is enlightening

indicators.note: putting one piece first places it at the front of the others
first says the second party comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: a revel is a lively party
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician who puts celebrating ahead of work is a revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revelatory reveals or discloses things, opening the mind and shedding light.

clue.text: Island overwhelmed by globalisation

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is swamped and buried, so the island sits buried in the longer word

explanation.surface: A small island's culture is swamped by global commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island, a well-known tourist destination.

clue.text: Tight covering originally taken off wound

indicators.note: taken off means removed, so a letter goes from the word for wound

parts.note: wound, rhyming with sound, means coiled, as a spring is wound

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of covering

explanation.surface: A tight bandage was removed from an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' and 'Tight' both pull towards bandages and injuries; wound is the past tense of wind, and tight means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for drunk, as is tight; well-oiled is the fuller phrase.

clue.text: 24's slower option perhaps while in transit

definitions.meaning: the winged horse in 24 across could fly, but a slower way to go is trotting on its hooves
an idiom for doing something while moving along, without stopping

explanation.surface: A winged horse might choose to walk, eating along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means done while travelling or busy with something else, like eating as you go.

clue.text: Trapped deer wandering onto crop

indicators.note: one piece put onto another follows it in an across answer

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

indicators.note: wandering suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stray deer is caught after straying into a field of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornered means trapped with no means of escape, like an animal backed into a corner.

clue.text: Speed ends up in Paris repackaged

indicators.note: repackaged means put together in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller's speedy trip finishes in Paris with its luggage repacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidness is quickness, the quality of moving fast.

clue.text: Charge Mark for posting Paradise Lost finally

parts.note: a stamp is a mark put on mail before posting

indicators.note: the final letter is lost, cut from the word for paradise

parts.note: Eden is the biblical paradise garden

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is charged for mailing a copy of Milton's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paradise Lost' looks like the Milton title, but 'Lost finally' drops the last letter of EDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a headlong charge, as of a panicking herd.

clue.text: Herman's other name for cheese

definitions.meaning: Herman ... is the Frankenstein-style father in the 1960s US sitcom The ...
a soft washed-rind cheese from Alsace

explanation.definitionFit: Munster is the surname of TV's Herman and also an Alsatian cheese, often spelt Muenster in the US.

clue.text: Muscular things overheard getting kisses

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by the ear, so the word is how it sounds

parts.note: pecs, the pectoral muscles of the chest

explanation.surface: Bodybuilders are overheard swapping kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: A peck is a quick light kiss, as on the cheek.

clue.text: Bread and butter maybe dunked into drink

indicators.note: something dunked into a drink is put inside it

parts.note: chai is Indian spiced tea
a pat is a small piece of butter, an example of a pat

explanation.surface: Someone dips buttered bread into a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened Indian flatbread.

clue.text: Live next to a new bit of 21 down

indicators.note: next to says the pieces sit side by side in this order

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Living next to a new money-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A bean is slang for a coin or a tiny sum, as in not having a bean, a bit of money.

clue.text: Large prize hard to return after comic's retirement

indicators.note: after puts the reversed pieces behind the comic

parts.note: a wit is a comic, someone funny

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: an award is a prize
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A comedian bows out, giving back a big award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' gives HDRAWAL from the three reversed pieces; 'retirement' is meant in its sense of pulling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal is a retreat or pulling back, a retirement from a position or activity.

clue.text: Brass curlew on garden fencing

indicators.note: fencing encloses, so the words wrap around the hidden answer

explanation.surface: A wading bird perches on the garden fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonga and brass are both British slang for money, cash.

clue.text: Extreme characters on river becoming quite blue

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at either end of the alphabet
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Letters at the edges of a river become rather blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky-blue colour, a shade that is very blue.

clue.text: Criminal got into part of Wandsworth

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar broke into a house in a south London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooting is a district in the London Borough of Wandsworth, in south London.

clue.text: Flier in continuous usage passed around

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the found letters run backwards
in says the letters are found within the clue's words

explanation.surface: A frequent flier has used something constantly over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds SUSAGEP across the words; 'around' turns it to read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the winged horse of Greek myth, a flying creature.

clue.text: Official in room feeding newborn?

indicators.note: feeding puts food into a mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a foal is a newborn horse

explanation.surface: An officer is found in a nursery feeding a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal means official or sanctioned, as in a formal statement.

clue.text: Aim high when half of pirate visible at last

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: half of takes the first half of the word pirate
at last picks the final letter of visible

explanation.surface: A pirate hopes for treasure when land finally comes into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set ambitious goals, aiming for success.
